week_thesis: Semiconductor sector suffered worst week in 18 years (SOX -11.4%) the week of Oct 12-16 on AI profitability concerns, China CXMT competition, and hot inflation data raising Fed rate-hike fears. Portfolio fell ~-5.8% WTD, down to ~$94,791. This Monday (Oct 19) premarket futures signal a semiconductor rebound (Nasdaq 100 +1.0%, S&P 500 +0.4%), but macro headwinds are not resolved. Strategy: execute the long-overdue DD close, then hold AMAT+NVDA (participating in today's semiconductor bounce) plus LLY (defensive ballast that preserved value during the semiconductor rout). No new semiconductor buys this week given SOX fragility — AMD still has Nov 3 earnings blackout, and MU at ~$931 (up from our $820 data) is no longer a clean dip buy. Big-tech earnings this week (META, TSLA) could clarify AI capex narrative.
